cards.title: Protect your first 90 minutes
cards.insight: Willpower and attention are highest early in the day. Spending the first block on reactive work (email, chat) trades your sharpest hours for other people's priorities.
cards.takeaway: Block the first 90 minutes for one meaningful task before opening any inbox.

cards.title: The two-minute rule
cards.insight: If a task takes under two minutes, doing it immediately is cheaper than tracking it. Small deferrals accumulate into a heavy mental backlog.
cards.takeaway: When something under two minutes appears, do it now instead of writing it down.

cards.title: Single-task to go faster
cards.insight: Context switching has a real reload cost; 'multitasking' is mostly rapid switching that fragments attention and slows every thread.
cards.takeaway: Close every tab and app not tied to your current task for one focused block.

cards.title: Define 'done' before you start
cards.insight: Open-ended tasks expand to fill available time. A concrete finish line turns an anxious, endless task into a bounded one.
cards.takeaway: Write one sentence describing what 'finished' looks like before beginning a task.
